what: catalogue 698: each of the desk's 27 tiles of frame 42 matched to a class of blind reading v3 from its shape alone, before the order file, the tile script, the frame or any letter was seen (plan v7-M, §8 step 3)

signs.note: a short upright stroke with a speck at its right and a low dash; smaller than any sign of the message; a stray mark, or what is left of one

a long upright stroke on the right with a foot at its lower right, joined at the top by a bar to a knotted loop at the upper left, and two blots joined by a stroke low on the left; like no class as a whole; perhaps a sign with a neighbour's trace
a dense knot at the top left and a stroke down to the right that ends in a short fork; like 9 turned over, whose tail runs down to the left; no class
a bar with two short strokes up at its left and a long slash down from its right end to the lower left
a thin stem under a slanted bar, not joined to it, with a dot at the bar's right end; T, but the bar slants and the dot stands to the right
a stem, an arm up to the right from its top, and a dot in the angle
faint and broken: an arc along the top with a knot at its right end, a dot in the middle, a slash low at the left; like S or 9 in parts; no class
a round ring at the left of a slash, joined to its top
a crossing at the top, a round bowl below curling back to the left, and strokes at the lower right that may be a neighbour's; K most like, 3 next
a closed loop at the top right of a stem, a short dash at the upper left, and a second stroke from the stem's foot up to the right; P in its loop and dot, with a stroke P lacks
a stem with a heavy bar across its top and a tick above the bar
a zigzag at the upper left and two parallel strokes down to the left through a bar: 3, turned
a bar along the top with a short stroke down at its left end, and a long slash from its right end down to the left; S without its foot, or 4 with its ticks turned down
a slash up from the lower left to a peaked loop at its upper right, with a dot at the upper left, and loose marks; P, or A if the loop is open
an upright stem, a roof from its top to the right that comes down in a second stem, and a dot between them; H in its roof, with a dot H has not shown

a three-cornered ring at the left joined to a stroke up to the right, and a long stroke down to the lower right; the ring is that of the doubtful Q (2:653, 2:717, 6:616, 5:285), but the long stroke runs down to the right, where Q's slash runs down to the left
a large open C with a stroke through its middle up to the right, blotted at the top
two strokes crossing at the top over a closed triangle with a leg down to the right; X above and Z's triangle below; no class
a spiral ring at the upper left, a stroke down at the right, and a base stroke from the lower left up to the right through it; 2 in its base, 9 or Q in its ring
two crossing strokes, the long one ending in a hook at the lower left, with a dot; as the X at 2:368
a heavy blotted slash with an angle opening to the lower right at its upper left; V if the angle is its wedge; the blot hides most of it
a tall stem with a foot, a bar to the right from its top, a dot under the bar; R, its arm flatter than R's
a short slash with a closed box on its right near the top; P, small and blotted
a ring lying on its side with a short stroke at its left and a dot below; like no class
a small blot with a short tail down to the right; too little to class
a slash with a filled ring at its left, joined near its top; Q with a filled ring, as at 1:545
a flat bar on top from a corner at its left, a stroke down from its right end that closes the top, a tail down to the lower left, and a dash to the right at the waist; Z, with 3's bar
